title.zh: LLM写作：让模型做编辑而非代笔
title.en: LLM Writing: Use Models as Editors

excerpt.zh: LLM写作的关键不是让模型替你下笔，而是先保留自己的初稿，再用模型机械地发现问题、检查结构并减少繁琐编辑。
excerpt.en: LLM writing works best when you keep authorship and use models to detect flaws, test structure, and handle tedious copyediting.

text.zh: LLM写作的核心：先写，再编辑
text.en: The Core of LLM Writing: Draft First, Edit Second

text.zh: LLM写作最稳妥的用法，不是让模型从零生成文章，而是先由作者完成初稿，再把模型当作严格的文案编辑。模型可以帮助发现重复、被动语态、名词化表达、冗余副词以及段落顺序问题，但文章的判断、观点和措辞仍应由作者掌握。
text.en: The safest approach to LLM writing is not to ask a model to generate an article from scratch. Write the first draft yourself, then use the model as a strict copyeditor. It can flag repetition, passive voice, nominalized language, unnecessary adverbs, and paragraphs that would work better elsewhere. The author should still control the judgment, ideas, and wording.

text.zh: 两条规则保护作者声音
text.en: Two Rules for Protecting the Author’s Voice

text.zh: 文章提出两条近乎苛刻的规则。第一，不直接采用模型建议的具体措辞，因为模型擅长生成顺滑、醒目的表达，却可能让整篇文章听起来像一串标题。第二，禁止模型用泛泛的鼓励掩盖问题。初稿往往需要重写结构、删减内容和重新思考，而不是被告知“整体很好”，否则作者可能误把初稿冲动当成成熟表达。
text.en: The article proposes two deliberately strict rules. First, do not directly adopt a specific phrase suggested by the model. Models are good at producing smooth, striking language, but that can make an entire article sound like a sequence of headlines. Second, do not let the model offer generic encouragement. Early drafts often need structural changes, cuts, and rethinking—not reassurance that everything already works.

text.zh: 把模型限制在机械而有价值的工作
text.en: Keep Models on Mechanical, Valuable Work

text.zh: 更有效的流程是把编辑拆成多轮检查：先让模型标出问题，再分别处理句子、段落和结构；需要比较改写时，尽量让不了解编辑过程的模型进行盲评，避免它因为知道作者刚改过文本而一味称赞。作者还建议建立自己的提示词清单，并用工具跟踪高亮、建议和版本变化，从而把重复劳动交给模型。
text.en: A more useful workflow breaks editing into passes: first ask the model to identify problems, then review sentences, paragraphs, and structure separately. When comparing revisions, use a model that does not know which version the author just changed, reducing the pressure to praise the latest edit. The author also recommends maintaining a personal checklist of prompts and using software to track highlights, suggestions, and revisions so repetitive work can be delegated.

text.zh: 这套方法的边界同样重要：模型的建议并不自动正确，甚至可能把文章改得过长、过度平滑或缺少个性。它最适合承担疲劳、规则明确的检查，而不适合决定作者究竟想说什么。最终的开放问题是，作者能否在获得效率的同时，持续抵抗模型的措辞和赞美；如果不能，所谓“编辑辅助”仍可能悄悄变成代笔。
text.en: Its limits matter just as much. Model suggestions are not automatically correct and may make prose longer, smoother, or less distinctive. Models are best suited to tiring, rule-based checks, not to deciding what the author means. The open question is whether writers can gain speed while resisting the model’s phrasing and praise. If they cannot, editing assistance may quietly become ghostwriting.
